answer: Web-activity clustering flags sybil identities that appear as a coordinated knoll of agent calls, not organic noise. After each epoch, the system compares each identity’s action timestamps against the global pulse of the agent pool; any identity whose behavior correlates above 0.8 with at least nine others is flagged for review. To overturn the flag, each identity in the cluster must submit unique HTTP fingerprints from distinct hardware, which costs an attacker one proxy setup per identity—plus a dawn of manual session resets to avoid repeating those fingerprints.
